headline: Public hearing on mobile home park lot rent increase rules; special elections for Charter Commission and Ward 3 council seat.
summary: First passage of an ordinance on lot rent increases in mobile home parks, along with a public hearing, is up for a vote. Two orders would set a special election for April 13, 2027, to pick six Charter Commission members and to fill the vacant Ward 3 council seat.
items: Public hearing and first passage on amendments to regulate lot rent increases in mobile home parks
Special election to elect six Charter Commission members
Special election to fill the vacant Ward 3 City Councilor seat

SUBJECT: 
 
Public Hearing and First Passage regarding amendments to the Administrative Ordinance, 
Business Ordinance, and Residential Rental Property Ordinance to regulate lot rent increases in 
mobile home parks.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
INFORMATION:  
 
On March 3, 2026, the City Council adopted a 180-day moratorium on lot rent increases for mobile 
home parks in Lewiston. The Lewiston Housing Committee was tasked with researching the topic 
of lot rent stabilization and drafting an ordinance for City Council’s consideration. With a draft in 
review with legal counsel, on August 26, 2026 City Council adopted a 180-day extension of the 
moratorium to provide sufficient time to finalize the draft ordinance that the City Council could 
consider and vote on.   
 
After completion of legal review and revisions, the City Council is asked to consider the draft 
ordinance for first passage.

AN ORDINANCE PERTAINING TO RENT STABILIZATION BOARD 
 
THE CITY OF LEWISTON HEREBY ORDAINS: 
 
Chapter 2 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Lewiston, Maine, is hereby amended as 
follows: 
 
CHAPTER 2  
 
ARTICLE IV. BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, COMMITTEES AND BUREAUS  
 
DIVISION 9. RENT STABILIZATION BOARD  
 
Sec. 2-235-A. Creation.  
A rent stabilization board is established and shall have the duties and authorities 
conferred by this ordinance. 
 
Sec. 2-235-B. Definitions.  
Terms defined in chapter 23, Article III shall apply to this division. 
 
Sec. 2-235-C. Membership  and Organization .  
(a) Members.  The rent stabilization board shall be comprised of three regular 
members, including a city employee who is a manager with expertise in business 
or financial matters, designated by the Administrator, two City residents, and two 
alternate members who are City residents. At least one of the City resident 
members or alternate members must have expertise in business or financial matters 
and one must have expertise in affordable housing, housing policy, housing 
planning, or housing stability. 
(b) Terms.  All appointed members of the rent stabilization board, other than the City 
employee shall serve staggered three-year terms from the date of their appointment 
and thereafter until their successors are appointed. At the time the initial 
appointments are made, the City Council shall assign each member to a term with 
one member appointed to a one-year term; one to a two-year term; and one to a 
three-year term. 
(c) Officers.  At an organizational meeting to be held annually, or at any other time by 
majority vote of its membership, the rent stabilization board shall select a chair 
and vice chair, who may perform the duties of the chair in the absence of the chair. 
(d) Alternate members.  Alternate members may participate and vote in rent 
stabilization board proceedings if a regular voting member is incapable or
No. 26- 
  Effective:   
 
2 
unavailable to serve at a particular meeting or is disqualified from participating in 
a particular matter because of a conflict of interest. The chair shall designate the 
alternate member to participate and vote on a matter. 
(e) Meetings.  The chair shall call meetings of the rent stabilization board as required. 
The chair shall also call meetings of the rent stabilization board when requested to 
do so by a majority of the members, the mayor, or a majority of the city council. A 
quorum necessary to conduct an official meeting of the rent stabilization board 
shall consist of at least two members or such alternate member or members 
designated by the chair. 
(f) Conflict of interest.  No person having a conflict of interest may serve as a 
regular member or alternate member of the rent stabilization board. A conflict of 
interest precluding service on the rent stabilization board shall include having an 
ownership interest in or employment role for any mobile home park, having an 
ownership interest in or employment role for any park owner, or being a mobile 
home resident. In the event that the City employee is disqualified from serving on 
the rent stabilization board under this paragraph, the Administrator shall designate 
another qualified City employee. 
Any questions of whether a member or alternate member has a conflict of interest 
sufficient to disqualify the member or alternate member shall be decided by a 
majority vote of the members present, except the member or alternate member 
whose possible conflict is being examined.  Where such vote results in a tie, the 
subject member or alternate member shall be disqualified. 
(g) Record.  The Administrator shall maintain a permanent record of all meetings of 
the rent stabilization board and all correspondence of the rent stabilization board. 
The Administrator shall be responsible for maintaining those records which are 
required as part of the various proceedings which may be brought before the rent 
stabilization board. The records of the rent stabilization board are presumed to be 
public records. 
(h) Application.  City residents interested in serving on the rent stabilization board 
shall apply to the city clerk and, from the applicants, the city council shall appoint 
two resident members and two alternate members. 
(i) Staff Support.  The Administrator shall assist the rent stabilization board with the 
preparation and posting of meeting agendas, the taking of minutes, and the drafting 
of correspondence or reports to the city council as needed. 
 
Sec. 2-235-D. Powers and duties .  
The rent stabilization board is authorized to:
No. 26-

3 
(a) Adopt such rules of procedure, consistent with law, charter and ordinance, as it 
shall determine is appropriate; 
(b) Adopt bylaws governing submission requirements for petitions for base rent 
increases in excess of the maximum annual increase or additional fee increases 
under section 23-303, consistent with law and ordinance; and 
(c) Adopt rules or regulations to ensure the fair and consistent consideration of 
petitions, under section 23-303, for an increase in base rent, greater than the 
maximum annual increase, or an additional fee, including in the application of the 
standards in section 23-303(d)(3), and to ensure the fair and consistent application 
of the Maintenance of Net Operating Income methodology. 
 
The rent stabilization board shall: 
(a) Act on petitions, under section 23-303, for an increase in base rent, greater than the 
maximum annual increase, or an additional fee; and, 
(b) The rent stabilization board shall submit a written report of its activities for the 
preceding year to the City Council on or before January 31 of each year.

THE CITY OF LEWISTON HEREBY ORDAINS:

BUSINESSES  
ARTICLE VIII. MOBILE HOME PARKS 
Sec. 22-221. License required to operate. 
(c) Application requirements: 
(1) Application for original licenses shall be made only after the proposed mobile 
home park has been approved by the planning board and shall be in writing, 
signed by the applicant as to the truth of the application, and accompanied by 
the deposit of a fee according to the business fee schedule as established by the 
city council; and such application shall contain: 
a. The name and address of the applicant; 
b. The location and legal description of the mobile home park; 
c. A site plan of the mobile home park showing all mobile home lots, 
structures, roads, walkways and other facilities. 
And in addition to the foregoing, the applicant shall furnish to the city clerk 
such other information as may be required by this article. 
(2) Applications for renewals of licenses shall be made in writing by holders of the 
licenses, shall be accompanied by the deposit of a fee according to the business 
fee schedule as established by the city council; and shall contain any change in 
the information submitted since the original license was issued or the latest 
renewal granted. 
(3) An applicant for a renewal license shall certify, on a form provided by the city 
clerk, that the applicant has fully complied with Article III, of chapter 23, at 
the mobile home park for the entire period of license for the prior year. 
If the applicant cannot certify full compliance, it shall certify full compliance 
other than each such event of noncompliance which it shall specifically detail.  
The applicant shall detail all persons harmed by any such event of 
noncompliance and suggest a complete remedy for each such event of 
noncompliance.

Sec. 22-224. Lot rent. 
(a) Moratorium Imposed. No mobile home park owner or manager may impose or 
implement an increase of lot rent on any person or entity who is a tenant of the 
mobile home park while this temporary moratorium is in effect. 
(a) Definitions. The following terms, wherever used in this ordinance, shall have the 
following meanings: 
Lot rent—The total amount owed, per month, to maintain a manufactured home, as 
defined in 10 M.R.S. § 9081, at a mobile home park, including, but not limited to, 
any mandatory, fixed charges or fees such as a connection, road maintenance, or 
recreation fee, but not including utility, telephone, or broadband expenses. 
Mobile home park—A parcel of land under unified ownership approved by the City of  
Lewiston or otherwise used for the placement of three (3) or more manufactured homes. 
(b) Applicability. This moratorium shall prevent the implementation of any increase in 
lot rent while this ordinance is in effect, regardless of whether the mobile home 
park owner or manager has previously informed the tenant of the mobile home 
park’s intent to increase the lot rent. 
(c) Duration. This moratorium shall become effective on the thirty-first (31st) day 
following its final passage by the city council (“Effective Date”) and shall remain 
in effect for a period of one hundred eighty (180) days from its Effective Date, 
unless extended, modified, or repealed by the City Council. 
(d) Purpose. The purpose of this moratorium is to allow the City Council sufficient 
time to study the causes and impacts of lot rent increases in mobile home parks 
and to consider and adopt appropriate amendments to the City’s ordinances. 
(e) Enforcement. This moratorium shall be enforced by the City of Lewiston 
Administrator or designee. 
(f) Penalties. Violation of any provision of this ordinance shall be punished by a civil 
penalty of $200.00 per offense. Each act of violation and every day upon which 
any such violation shall occur shall constitute a separate offense. Should the City 
prevail in any action to enforce this ordinance, the City may recover its costs of 
suit, including reasonable attorney's fees. 
(g) Severability. If any portion of this ordinance is declared invalid or unconstitutional 
by a court of competent jurisdiction, such declaration shall not affect the validity 
of the remaining portions of the ordinance.

AN ORDINANCE PERTAINING TO MOBILE PARK RENT STABILIZATION 
 
THE CITY OF LEWISTON HEREBY ORDAINS: 
 
Chapter 23 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Lewiston, Maine, is hereby amended as 
follows: 
 
CHAPTER 23  
RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTY  
ARTICLE  III. MOBILE HOME PARK RENT STABILIZATION ORDINANCE  
Sec. 23-300.- Purpose 
The purpose of this ordinance is to protect residents living in mobile home parks 
from unreasonable lot rent and fee increases. Many mobile home residents own their 
mobile home and rent a mobile home park lot.  Mobile homes can be difficult and 
expensive to move from one parcel of land to another.  Mobile home parks represent a 
source of unsubsidized affordable housing, and mobile home park residents are 
particularly vulnerable to unreasonable rent and fee increases. This ordinance 
establishes a review process to ensure that rent and fee increases ar e reasonably tied to 
increases in the Consumer Price Index and a mobile home park’s increased costs in 
maintaining and improving the park.  
 
Sec 23-301.- Definitions 
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the 
meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a 
different meaning: 
Additional Fees means any charges not included in the definition of base rent that a 
park owner demands of a mobile home resident, or that a mobile home resident pays to a park 
owner. Additional fees may include a capital expense. 
Administrator means the municipal official responsible for the administration and 
enforcement of this mobile home park rent stabilization ordinance. The Administrator shall be 
the City Administrator or the City Administrator‘s designee. 
Base Rent means the total amount of rent and fees charged by a park owner for any 
mobile home park lot as of a specific date. Base rent shall include any charge for rent or fees 
regardless of whether the rent or fees are stated as a lump sum or itemized separately.  Base 
rent may include a capital expense. 
Capital expense means any expenditure made by a park owner to fund the cost of a 
capital improvement.
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
2 
Capital improvement means any permanent addition, renovation, or structural 
improvement to the mobile home park that is properly capitalized under generally accepted 
accounting principles (GAAP) rather than expensed as a routine operating cost, and that (1) 
materially extends the useful life of the park or its infrastructure, (2) increases the value or 
functionality of the park as a whole, or (3) adds a new amenity or facility. 
A capital improvement does not include routine maintenance; replacement of 
individual components due to normal wear and tear; work necessitated, in whole or in 
material part, by the park owner's failure to perform timely and adequate maintenance; repairs 
that restore an item to its prior condition without extending its useful life; administrative or 
overhead expenses; or any cost the park owner is already legally obligated to bear as a 
condition of maintaining a habitable premises under state law or city ordinance. 
Consumer Price Index (also called CPI) means the Consumer Price Index for the 
Northeast Region, or its successor index, as published by the United States Department of 
Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics, as published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of 
Labor Statistics, or its successor agency. 
Cooperative means a domestic corporation that is organized under or elects to be 
governed by the provisions of 13 M.R.S. §§ 1741 - 1764 or other entity in which park 
ownership is limited to mobile home residents, and in which all mobile home residents in 
good standing have the option to become owners of the mobile home park with equal 
membership rights in the ownership structure. 
Fees means charges to a mobile home resident by a park owner for water, sewer, solid 
waste disposal or grounds maintenance costs. 
Lawful vacancy means a licensed mobile home park lot that is not being possessed 
by a mobile home resident and for which the base rent and additional fees, if any, are not 
being demanded by the park owner of a current or future mobile home resident, and for 
which the base rent and additional fees, if any, are not being paid by a current or future 
mobile home resident. The following events are included in the definition of lawful 
vacancy:  
(1) A mobile home lot becomes unoccupied due to an act of the park owner to 
terminate a lease for a mobile home resident’s non-payment of the base rent or 
additional fee; or 
(2) A mobile home lot becomes unoccupied due to an act of the mobile home 
resident’s choosing to terminate their lease or not renew their lease, and 
subsequently moving off a mobile home lot.  
The following events shall not constitute a lawful vacancy: 
(1) A lot becomes unoccupied due to an act of the park owner to terminate a lease, 
refuse the renewal of a lease, or issue a notice to quit to a mobile home resident 
for any reason other than non-payment of the base rent or additional fee;
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
3 
(2) An existing mobile home resident in the park sells that resident’s mobile home 
to a new mobile home resident and the new mobile home resident then begins 
to occupy the existing mobile home on the same lot, including when such an 
event causes a temporary period in which the mobile home is unoccupied; and, 
(3) An event in which the repair or replacement of an existing mobile home 
requires a mobile home resident’s temporary absence from such mobile 
home, so long as that mobile home resident continues to pay base rent and 
additional fees, if any, to the park owner.  At the request of a mobile home 
resident, if that mobile home resident and park owner agree to a relocation 
schedule in which the mobile home resident moves their mobile home or 
builds a new mobile home on a different lot in the same mobile home park 
which is comparable in size and character to that mobile home resident’s 
current lot, this relocation shall not, in any way, void the base rent.  If the 
mobile home resident’s relocation requires that the mobile home resident 
temporarily occupy two or more lots at the same time, that mobile home 
resident may be charged accordingly for the occupancy of those mobile 
home park lots until one or more mobile home park lots are fully vacated, at 
which time the mobile home resident shall only be charged for the mobile 
home park lot the mobile home resident continues to occupy.  
Maximum Annual Increase means the lesser of (i) the posted annual percentage 
change in the CPI for the 12-month period, ending with the month the notice is provided, plus 
one percentage point (1%), and (ii) five percent (5%). 
Mobile Home means a structure, transportable in one or more sections, which is 8 body 
feet or more in width and 32 body feet or more in length, is built on a permanent chassis, is 
designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the 
required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning and electrical systems 
contained in the structure. 
Mobile Home Park means any parcel(s) of land under single or common ownership or 
control which contains, or is designed, laid out or adapted to accommodate, two or more 
mobile homes. 
Mobile Home Park Lot means the area of land on which an individual mobile home is 
situated within a mobile home park and which is reserved for use by the occupants of that mobile 
home. 
Mobile Home Resident means an occupant of a mobile home who rents a mobile home 
park lot.  
Park Owner means an individual, a corporation or other entity that owns a mobile 
home park. 
Rent means charges to a mobile home resident by a park owner for the temporary 
possession and use of a mobile home park lot.
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
4 
Rent Increase means any additional base rent or additional fees demanded of, or paid by, 
a mobile home resident, and includes any reduction in services without a corresponding 
reduction in the amount demanded or paid for in base rent or additional fees. 
Rent Stabilization Board means the municipal body established by chapter 2, 
article IV, division 9, of this Code. 
 
Sec. 23-302 - Requirements of All Parks Owners 
(a) Limitation on number of base rent and additional fee increases.  A park owner 
may not implement an increase in base rent or an additional fee more than once per 
calendar year.   
(b) Notice Requirements.  A park owner shall provide notice of any increase in base 
rent or an additional fee to the affected mobile home residents after the rent 
stabilization board acts on any petition under section 23-303, if one is filed, and no 
less than 90 days before the effective date of the increase. The notice shall include: 
(1) The name, address, telephone number and e-mail address of the park owner;  
(2) The amount of the increase in base rent, if any;  
(3) The amount of the increase in fees, if any, and the type of fee increase; and 
(4) Any other information required by a state law, including 10 M.R.S. §9093-B(2). 
 
Sec. 23-303.- Base Rent and Additional Fee Increase Limitations 
(a) Applicability.  This section shall apply to any park owner. 
(b) Base Rent.  A park owner shall not demand, accept or retain base rent for a mobile 
home park lot that exceeds the base rent as provided for herein.  
(1) The amount of a base rent increase for a prospective period shall be determined 
by multiplying the current base rent by the maximum annual increase or a 
lesser amount. 
(2) A park owner may increase base rent whenever a lawful vacancy occurs, and 
this amount shall be considered the new base rent for that mobile home park 
lot without a requirement to petition the rent stabilization board. Any new base 
rent set pursuant to this paragraph shall be subject to all limitations, formulas, 
and procedural requirements for future base rent increases contained in this 
section. 
(3) Exemption.  The park owner is exempt from this subsection and has no 
requirement to petition the rent stabilization board to increase the base rent, for 
a particular lot, if the new base rent proposed in a notice sent pursuant to 
section 23-302 is less than the product of 0.34 of Fair Market Rent at the time
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
5 
the notice is issued, rounded to the nearest whole dollar.  For the avoidance of 
doubt, as of the effective date of this ordinance, the product of 0.34 and current 
Fair Market Rent equals $570. 
(c) Additional Fees.  Except as provided herein, a park owner shall not demand, 
accept or retain additional fees that exceed the additional fees on the effective date 
of this ordinance. A park owner that seeks to impose a new or increased additional 
fee shall petition and obtain advance approval for the fee from the rent 
stabilization board. 
(d) Petition for Increase In Base Rent, Greater Than the Maximum Annual 
Increase, or Additional Fees. A park owner seeking to increase base rent, greater 
than the maximum annual increase, or an additional fee must submit a petition to 
the rent stabilization board. A park owner may seek an increase in base rent, 
greater than the maximum annual increase, or an additional fee because of the cost 
of increased operating expenses such as taxes, insurance, utility charges and 
maintenance costs; and/or the cost of capital expenses, in excess of those 
accounted for in the base rent, that directly benefit mobile home residents.   
(1) The complete petition must be filed more than 157 days prior to the effective 
date of the proposed increase and contain documentation that the increase is 
necessary to cover increased operating expenses or the cost of eligible capital 
improvements.  The petition shall include a petition fee, in accordance with the 
schedule as established by the city council. 
(2) The city clerk shall determine whether the petition is complete.  If the 
Administrator determines that a submitted petition is not complete, the 
petitioner shall be notified within fourteen (14) days after receipt of the 
petition of the additional information required to process the petition. If such 
additional information is not submitted within thirty (30) days of the city 
clerk’s request, or such later time that the city clerk provides, the petition shall 
be deemed to be denied. If the city clerk determines the application is 
complete, the city clerk shall notify the petitioner and the rent stabilization 
board. 
(3) Standards. 
a. Standard for petition based on increased operating expenses.  A 
park owner petitioning for a base rent increase in excess of the 
maximum annual increase or an additional fee increase based in whole 
or in part on increased operating expenses must demonstrate to the rent 
stabilization board that there are actual and reasonable operating 
expenses in excess of the maximum annual increase allowed that are 
necessary to maintain the existing level of services to the mobile home
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
6 
park residents or that are necessary to implement an increase in services 
that will have a direct benefit to the mobile home park residents. 
b. Standard for petition based on increased eligible capital expenses.  
A park owner petitioning for a base rent increase in excess of the 
maximum annual increase or an additional fee increase based in whole 
or in part on increased eligible capital expenses must demonstrate to the 
rent stabilization board: 
(1) That the capital improvement will have a direct benefit to the 
mobile home park residents;  
(2) The total capital outlay required for the capital improvement;  
(3) The useful life of the capital improvement, as determined by 
generally accepted accounting principles or IRS depreciation 
schedules;  
(4) The total rate of return on the capital outlay over the useful life 
of the improvement calculated as the prevailing yield on ten-
year U.S. Treasury securities plus two (2) percentage points, as 
published by the Federal Reserve at the time petition is filed; 
and  
(5) The proposed base rent or additional fee increase calculated as 
the total capital outlay plus the total amount of the of return on 
capital divided by the useful life of the capital improvement 
divided by the number of sites in the mobile home park 
specified in the park’s license issued pursuant to 10 M.R.S. 
§9082 of the Manufactured Housing Act.  
c. Additional Standard for a petition for an additional fee increase.  A 
park owner seeking an additional fee increase shall have the additional 
burden of demonstrating to the rent stabilization board: 
(1) That the requested increase is not accounted for in the base rent; 
and 
(2) That any additional fee is directly related to and proportionate 
to costs incurred by the park owner for providing the service 
funded by the additional fee. 
d. It is expected that a base rent increase or an additional fee increase 
allowed pursuant to one or more of the foregoing subsections will 
provide the park owner with a fair and reasonable return on 
investment.  However, in the event that a base rent increase or an 
additional fee increase allowed pursuant to one or more of the 
foregoing subsections does not provide a park owner with a fair and
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
7 
reasonable return on investment, the park owner may request an 
increase in base rent greater than the maximum annual increase or an 
additional fee increase by filing a petition in accordance with the rent 
stabilization board’s bylaws, rules and regulations.  The rent 
stabilization board may approve an increase in base rent greater than 
the maximum annual increase or an additional fee increase, after notice 
and hearing on a complete petition, as it determines necessary to ensure 
a fair and reasonable return on investment. 
For the purposes of this ordinance, a fair and reasonable return on 
investment must be calculated using Maintenance of Net Operating 
Income methodology, as that term is used in other jurisdictions with 
similar ordinances, that presumes that the net operating income the park 
owner earned during April 2025 through March 2026 yielded a fair 
return, unless the park owner proves that special or peculiar 
circumstances prevented the park owner from receiving a fair return on 
investment during that period.  
e. The park owner shall bear the burden of demonstrating with competent 
evidence to the rent stabilization board that a base rent increase or an 
additional fee increase is necessary. 
(4) The rent stabilization board may approve, approve with conditions or deny a 
park owner’s petition, as provided in this subsection.  Every final decision of 
the rent stabilization board shall include written findings of fact. The rent 
stabilization board shall act upon the application before the 61st day after the 
city clerk determines that the petition is complete.  If the rent stabilization 
board does not act before the 61st day, the petition shall be deemed to be 
approved. 
 
Sec. 23-304.- Enforcement 
(a) Notice of Violation.  The Administrator is authorized to serve a notice of violation 
or order on the person responsible for violating a provision of this article or who 
shall fail to comply with any of the requirements hereof.  A notice of violation 
shall be served in the manner set forth in section 50-43. 
(b) Requests for Appeal.  Any person served a notice of violation or order, pursuant 
to this section, may request a hearing before the rent stabilization board by filing a 
written petition and fee, in accordance with the schedule as established by the city 
council, for said hearing at the Executive Department within ten (10) days of the 
date of service of the notice of violation or order. The rent stabilization board may 
sustain, modify, or withdraw such notice of violation or order.
No. 26- 
  Effective:  
 
8 
(c) Civil infraction and civil penalties.  Any person failing to comply with a notice 
of violation or order served in accordance with this section shall be deemed guilty 
of a civil infraction and the violation shall be deemed a strict liability offense.  
Each day that a violation continues after due notice has been served shall be 
deemed a separate offense.  The penalty for a specific violation is $100. 
(d) Any person who shall violate a provision of this article or who shall fail to comply 
with any of the requirements hereof, shall be liable for one or more citations as set 
forth in Chapter 1, Section 1-8 and Chapter 50, Section 50-36 of the Code of 
Ordinances of the City of Lewiston.  In lieu of or in addition to the issuance of 
citations under Lewiston ordinance, the Administrator may initiate a civil violation 
citation pursuant to Rule 80H of the Maine Rules of Civil Procedure. 
 
Sec. 23-305.- Applicability 
This ordinance applies to every mobile home park within the City. 
 
Sec. 23-306.- Appeals 
Decisions of the rent stabilization board may be appealed to Superior Court by park owners 
or affected mobile home residents. 
Appeals as described herein shall be filed with the Superior Court in accordance 
with Maine Rule of Civil Procedure 80B within 45 days of the decision made by the rent 
stabilization board. Appeals must be based solely on the record of the proceedings before 
the rent stabilization board. The record on appeal shall include the petition; the minutes and 
any audio or video recordings of rent stabilization board meetings related to the petition; all 
exhibits, papers, applications, and requests submitted to the rent stabilization board; and the 
final written decision of the rent stabilization board.

ORDER, ESTABLISHING THE DATE FOR A SPECIAL ELECTION TO ELECT SIX 
MEMBERS OF THE CHARTER COMMISSION 
 
Whereas,  at the November 3, 2026 municipal election, the voters approved Ballot Question 2 which 
calls for the establishment of a Charter Commission to create a new Municipal Charter; 
and 
Whereas,  the state statutes define the process for the membership of the Charter Commission, 
notably three members to be appointed by the City Council and six members to be 
elected at large; and 
Whereas,  the City Council desires to have the process begin as soon as feasible rather than waiting 
for the next regular municipal election in November 2027, 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered, that the City Council calls for a special municipal election to be held on 
Tuesday, April 13, 2027 for the election of six residents to serve as at-large members of the Charter 
Commission, and directs the City Clerk to administer the election per the state statute regulations.

CITY COUNCIL ORDER 
November 24, 2026 
 
ORDER, ESTABLISHING THE DATE FOR A SPECIAL ELECTION TO FILL THE VACANT 
POSITION OF WARD 3 CITY COUNCILOR 
 
Whereas,  City Councilor Scott Harriman has resigned his position, effective December 4, 2026, and 
Whereas,  the City Charter calls for an open seat on the City Council to be filled by a special 
election if there is more than six months remaining in the term, and 
Whereas,  the City Council desires to hold the special election in conjunction with the special 
election for the Charter Commission,  
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered, that the City Council calls for a special municipal election to be held on 
Tuesday, April 13, 2027 for the election of a Ward 3 City Councilor, and directs the City Clerk to 
administer said election.
